question: Should a 5-person startup use cloud LLM APIs or self-host an open-source model?

plan.main_question: Should a 5-person startup use cloud LLM APIs or self-host an open-source model?
plan.decision_context: The engineering leads of a 5-person startup need to choose between cloud LLM APIs and self-hosting open-source models, balancing limited engineering bandwidth against infrastructure costs and data privacy needs.

subquestions.question: What are the total cost of ownership differences between high-volume cloud LLM APIs and self-hosting open-source models on cloud GPUs for a small team?
subquestions.success_criteria: Comparative cost breakdown including token pricing versus GPU instance hourly rates and maintenance overhead.

subquestions.success_criteria: Clear outline of DevOps requirements, tooling needed like vLLM or TGI, and maintenance hours for self-hosting.

subquestions.question: What are the performance and latency benchmarks of leading cloud LLM APIs versus self-hosted open-source models of comparable size?

subquestions.question: What data privacy, compliance, and security risks are involved with cloud LLM APIs versus fully self-hosted infrastructure?
subquestions.success_criteria: Analysis of data retention policies for major API providers compared to complete data ownership in self-hosted environments.

self hosted LLM data security benefits

decision.rationale: All three specialists are required to thoroughly cover the financial, technical, and risk aspects of the cloud versus self-hosted infrastructure decision for a small startup.

summaries.sq1: For teams of fewer than ten engineers, hosted LLM APIs provide a lower total cost of ownership below a threshold of several billion tokens per month [ev11]. Engineering labor required to maintain self-hosted models in production accounts for 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer [ev9], which outweighs compute savings until high-volume thresholds are met [ev10]. At lower volumes (e.g., 40 million tokens per month), monthly API spend for small models stays under $500 [ev12], and variable pricing eliminates fixed monthly costs during early product-market fit search [ev13].

summaries.sq2: Self-hosting open-source LLMs requires significant ongoing engineering effort (estimated at 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer) [ev3]. Teams face infrastructure challenges such as driver updates breaking containers [ev17], out-of-memory crashes from long prompts [ev18], and constant monitoring needs [ev19]. In contrast, integrating cloud APIs eliminates infrastructure maintenance and infrastructure expertise requirements.
summaries.sq3: Dedicated GPU deployments for open-source models achieve a median time-to-first-token of approximately 120 milliseconds for short prompts [ev15]. Shared cloud APIs range between 250 and 600 milliseconds, and their 99th percentile latency can reach several seconds during peak hours [ev16].

summaries.sq4: Major hosted AI providers do not use business API data for model training by default [ev1], but typically retain prompts and outputs for up to 30 days for abuse detection [ev2], and may require a signed data processing agreement for zero-retention options [ev3]. Utilizing third-party APIs means data leaves internal infrastructure [ev4], requiring outsourcing risk assessments, data residency checks, and compliance notifications [ev7]. Conversely, fully self-hosted infrastructure keeps data entirely within the organization's control [ev5], though it places the full burden of access controls, security patching, audit logging, and incident response onto the internal team [ev5, ev8]. In both deployment models, the organization remains fully responsible for its compliance and data handling obligations [ev6, ev8].

agreements: Hosted APIs provide lower total cost of ownership and minimal fixed costs for low to moderate token volumes [ev11, ev12, ev13, ev14].
Self-hosting requires ongoing engineering labor, maintenance, and monitoring resources [ev9, ev10, ev17, ev18, ev19].

report.title: Cloud LLM APIs Versus Self-Hosting Open-Source Models for a 5-Person Startup
report.executive_summary: A 5-person startup should use cloud LLM APIs rather than self-hosting open-source models. Cloud APIs offer a lower total cost of ownership and have zero fixed monthly costs at low-to-moderate token volumes, whereas self-hosting demands significant engineering labor and constant infrastructure maintenance that strains a small team. This decision depends heavily on maintaining low token volumes and standard data privacy requirements that do not mandate strict on-premise infrastructure.

findings.statement: For organizations with fewer than ten engineers, keeping a self-hosted model reliable requires 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer.
Hosted APIs provide lower total cost of ownership below a threshold of several billion tokens per month.
For a median startup team processing 40 million tokens per month, monthly API spend stays under $500 for small models and between $800 and $2,500 for frontier models.
Cloud APIs feature pay-as-you-go pricing with no fixed monthly costs, scaling down to near zero when usage is low.
Self-hosting can lead to unexpected downtime, out-of-memory crashes, and high maintenance overhead for small teams lacking dedicated infrastructure engineers.
Most major hosted AI providers do not use business API data for model training by default, though they commonly retain data for up to 30 days for abuse detection.

limitations: Evidence regarding the day-to-day operational horror stories relies heavily on forum anecdotes with lower source quality.
Specific proprietary infrastructure benchmarks may vary depending on the exact cloud provider and hardware utilized.
report.recommendation: Use cloud LLM APIs now to preserve engineering bandwidth and minimize fixed costs while searching for product-market fit; revisit self-hosting only when token volume consistently approaches several billion per month or if strict regulatory mandates require total data localization.
